seasons.review_body: The Good Bad Mother aired on JTBC in April 2023 and quietly became one of the most-talked-about Korean dramas of the year, earning a spot on Time magazine's 10 Best Korean Dramas of 2023 on Netflix. The premise - a ruthless prosecutor, felled by a near-fatal accident, regresses to the mind of a child and must relearn the world alongside the mother he resented - sounds melodrama-adjacent, but the execution is rawer than the logline suggests. NME's Carmen Chin called it "unapologetically raw and heartfelt," noting the rapport between Ra Mi-ran and Lee Do-hyun feels "terrifyingly authentic." The series set records for JTBC's Wednesday-Thursday slot and collected multiple Baeksang Arts Award nominations. Its 8.4 IMDb score and 90% audience approval on Rotten Tomatoes reflect an unusually broad emotional consensus: viewers who came for the family drama stayed for its unsentimental reckoning with ambition, sacrifice, and the gap between the parent a child needs and the parent survival produces.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Young-soon's unyielding parenting philosophy and Kang-ho's hollow, transactional adulthood with an efficiency that makes the coming rupture feel inevitable. Ra Mi-ran commands every frame.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Young-soon's quiet collapse behind the barn after her son dismisses her - the show's emotional key set in the first hour.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 14
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers what Korean family dramas rarely manage: earned resolution that does not sand off the show's harder edges. The mother-son arc closes with a specificity that bypasses sentimentality.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Young-soon and an adult Kang-ho sharing a meal on the farm - the show's thesis landing without a single line of dialogue.
